# 3 Maccabees Chapter 3 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Alexandrinus) | **Section:** The Royal Decree Against the Jews

---

**1** When Ptolemy learned of this situation and was informed that the Jews were firmly resolved and would not submit to his edicts, having heard further that some were favorably disposed toward him and that many were devoted to him, he gave orders that no change in their attitude should be made, and that they should be held in custody under guard, bound in iron chains on every side, and given no assistance or comfort of any kind.

**2** Moreover by his command they were stripped of all their possessions and rights of citizenship.

**3** They were not permitted to draw water from wells or to receive any of the other benefits of life.

**4** All this was accomplished by means of royal decrees, as befits a king bereft of reason and wisdom.

**5** But when these things became known to the Jews' friends, since many of the Alexandrians had friendly relations with them, they visited them secretly, bringing provisions and consoling them.

**6** They raised the Jews' spirits with the hope that things would change, and the Alexandrians also promised to do whatever was in their power to arrange their release.

**7** Then Ptolemy issued further orders, commanding that the whole nation of Jews be gathered into one place and brought to him under guard.

**8** He also commanded that any persons of standing who refused to comply with his orders regarding the Jews and sought to help them in any way should be put to death.

**9** When these measures had been carried out and great violence had been inflicted on the Jews, there arose among all the people of Judea a strong desire to help the Jews and stand with them.

**10** Then the king, puffed up with arrogance and intoxicated with the power of his position, wrote as follows.

**11** King Ptolemy Philopator to the commanders and soldiers throughout Egypt and all its territories, greetings. I am in good health and my affairs are proceeding well.

**12** Since the expedition to Asia has concluded and we have returned safely through the goodwill of the gods and the favor of fortune, we have now determined, not through force but through benevolence, to devote ourselves to the service of the land's gods.

**13** However, since the Jews continue to show ill will toward us and have refused to submit to our rule, treating our sacred places with contempt and stirring up trouble in our kingdom,

**14** we have resolved to deal with them accordingly and to make them answer publicly for their insolent behavior.

**15** Therefore we instruct you as follows: all the Jews in your territory are to be arrested and transported to Alexandria, to be brought to us under guard.

**16** They are to receive no compassion or mercy whatsoever.

**17** We are confident that these enemies of our authority have been subdued and that our power over them is complete.

**18** On their arrival in Alexandria they are to be executed by torture and death.

**19** In this way we will eradicate this entire people from among us.

**20** All their property is to be confiscated for the royal treasury.

**21** Any person who shelters a Jew will be put to death.

**22** We are sending copies of this letter throughout the land so that it may be known to all, and all may be prepared to carry out our command without exception or delay.
